text:
incidents-bot: [ALERT] Elevated p99 tail latency on streaming endpoints (/v1/stream) starting ~10:40UTC, automatic page to on-call. Severity: P2.
Alice: I'm on it, acknowledging page. digging into metrics.
Ben: Pulling proxy and worker stats now. seeing write stalls from edge -> backend connections. p95 ~600ms, p99 ~7.8s, error rate slightly up.
Carla: Which customers impacted? Sarah-CS, can you surface any live reports?
Sarah-CS: Two enterprise tenants reported slow/partial streams, roughly 2% of active streaming sessions in EU region. No ticket yet, creating one and notifying account teams. :wave:
Alice: Reproduced local trace: client open SSE, server generates tokens but they're buffered at proxy layer; backend logs show steady output. suspect proxy write backpressure + long keepalive.
Ben: Grep from proxy logs: `grep "write blocked" /var/log/edge/proxy.log | tail -n 50` shows recurring EAGAIN and queue growth on socket writes.
Dave: Paging in edge-proxy-bot to confirm config state. @edge-proxy-bot what are current write_timeout/write_buffer values?
edge-proxy-bot: Current config (eu-edge): write_timeout=120s, send_buffer=512KB, max_concurrent_streams=2000, keepalive=300s. Last rollout: 2028-01-14.
Carla: That send_buffer seems large; combined with slow consumers this can amplify head-of-line stalls. Suggest lowering send_buffer and enabling early-flush for SSE.
Ben: Quick mitigation options I can do now: 1) reduce send_buffer to 64KB on a small EU canary pool 2) decrease write_timeout to 30s 3) enable aggressive client eviction for idle streams. Can roll in 5m.
Alice: While Ben prepares canary, I'll enable prefix/KV cache bypass for streaming route to avoid extra buffering, and add metric to measure socket backpressure events.
Matt-oncall: Agree with canary. Make sure autopolicy fallback to non-streaming (long-poll) is ready if we need to divert. Notify ops if we flip fallback.
Ben: Canary deploy started to 10% of EU edge nodes. watch metrics: p99 dropping from 7.8s -> 1.4s on canary within 90s. No increased errors so far.
Carla: Good sign. Prepare runbook step to roll to 100% if stable for 10m, otherwise revert. Document change in rollback ticket.
Sarah-CS: Informing affected accounts that we're mitigating; customer impact: intermittent stalls and partial payloads for streaming sessions, estimated 2% sessions, ETA to resolution TBD.
Alice: Root cause hypothesis: large proxy send buffer + long write_timeout + slow consumer connections (mobile clients on flaky networks) causing buffer bloat; when buffer fills, socket write blocks cascade into backend stalls and increased p99.
Ben: After 10m canary, metrics look stable. Rolling changes to remaining EU nodes now with 5m stagger.
edge-proxy-bot: Rollout to eu-edge nodes: started.
Dave: Alerting infra to hold autoscaling triggers -- we may hit transient CPU while proxies flush.
Matt-oncall: Good mitigation. Incident summary for pager: cause = proxy-side buffer bloat + slow clients; mitigation = reduced send_buffer, shorter write_timeout, aggressive idle eviction, canary + rollout; customer impact = ~2% streaming sessions, degraded p99 up to 8s, now trending down.
Carla: Create post-incident action items: (1) add backpressure metric to SLO dashboards, (2) consider adaptive send_buffer per client pattern, (3) add consumer-side guidance to docs.
Sarah-CS: Sending update to account teams and creating incident ticket for affected tenants.
Alice: Handoff to night on-call (Matt) in 30m. I'll leave notes + links to dashboards and the rollout change ID: `roll-eu-2028-04-23-42`.
Matt-oncall: Acknowledged. I'll monitor next 2 hours, escalate if p99 > 2s or error rate > 1%. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
incidents-bot: Incident P2 downgraded to Watch. Recorded incident ID INC-2028-0423-7.
